research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google: Nano Banana 2 renders short legible text well; structure prompts as subject, composition, action, setting, style; concrete composition and lighting beat adjectives
https://fal.ai/learn/tools/how-to-use-nano-banana-2 — naming an era or medium makes the model infer grain, colour and period composition on its own; useful for cheap-film night looks
https://morphed.app/blog/nano-banana-2-prompts — short text (1-4 words) in quotes renders most reliably (vendor claim, unverified); keep the number to one short string
https://fliki.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — name a specific film stock, lens and light source rather than 'cinematic'
https://www.lifehacker.com.au/?p=1060791 — size-comparison videos work through the relation between objects and a familiar reference (a person beside the giant), not the objects alone

https://the-dots.com/projects/home-truths-90048 — Home Truths (London): empty homes vs homelessness shown as 3D-printed sculptural data maps and a fold-out map; the physical model is an established way in

https://www.citylab.com/housing/2017/04/learning-from-two-months-of-illuminating-abandoned-homes/523317/ — Breathing Lights lit vacant houses' windows; light in an empty window reads strongly, but audiences can misread it as celebration, so keep the empties dark and the lit thing the households
https://www.goethe.de/ins/gb/en/m/kul/past/glei/liv/21152755.html — empty England pictured as Victorian brick terraces in Liverpool and Manchester; boarded rows are the recognisable image

https://www.safesitefacilities.co.uk/case-studies/sitex-steel-security-screens-southampton — long-term voids in England are sealed with grey perforated steel security screens over windows and doors: the specific, un-generic signifier of an empty English home
https://live.historicengland.org.uk/advice/planning/housing/low-demand-housing — whole streets of terraced houses empty and boarded in the Midlands and north
notes: Beat C must make the 134,210 households (beat B) suddenly small. All three keep the empties DARK and the households as the only warm-cold teal light, so the eye measures the ratio. a = the literal true-scale comparison (aerial, ratio of lit to dark roughly 1:2.3). b = the surprise: the empties as house keys on an office wall, no houses at all. c = a physical data model on a trestle table, the Home Truths approach, with the one number written. English specifics: brick terraces, grey perforated steel window screens, wheelie bins, sodium-free fluorescent teal. Film language from the reference: night, cheap colour negative, grain, cold fluorescent teal, lonely. Only image c carries text: '303,185'.

stills.look: The dark city of empties (aerial true scale)
stills.prompt: Vertical 9:16 aerial photograph at night, looking straight down from very high over an endless grid of English Victorian brick terraced streets, rows of slate roofs and back yards running to the edge of the frame in every direction, every house dark, windows sealed with grey perforated steel security screens, no lights on anywhere. In the lower left corner, one small patch of the grid glows cold fluorescent teal: a few streets of tiny lit windows, small enough to cover with a thumb, utterly outnumbered by the darkness around it. Shot on cheap 35mm colour negative film pushed two stops, heavy grain, slight halation round the teal, faint motion blur, no people visible. Thanks.

stills.look: The key wall (every empty house as a key)
stills.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photograph at night inside a shabby English lettings office after closing, a single flickering fluorescent tube overhead throwing cold teal light. The whole back wall, floor to ceiling and receding down a long corridor into darkness, is pegboard hung with thousands upon thousands of identical brass Yale-style house keys on small paper tags, each one for a house nobody lives in, dust on the tags, keys untouched for months. At the bottom of the frame, on a worn grey carpet tile, one small cardboard box of a few keys, lit brighter, looking tiny against the wall. No people. Cheap colour negative film, grain, slight green-teal cast, lonely and eerie. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 photograph at night in an empty English community hall, folding chairs stacked against the wall, one fluorescent strip light overhead casting cold teal. On a long trestle table stretching away from camera sits a vast architectural model: rows and rows of tiny unpainted grey card terraced houses packed shoulder to shoulder to the far end of the table and spilling onto a second table, every one dark. In the near corner a much smaller cluster of tiny model figures, lit teal, dwarfed. A hand-lettered card propped at the front reads "303,185". Shot on cheap colour negative film with a 35mm lens, low angle, shallow depth of field, heavy grain, scuffed lino floor. Thanks.
